definition: Durability means the ability to withstand wear, damage, or rough use over a long time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word durability. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know durability should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Elena chose her hiking boots for their durability; after five years of rocky trails, the stitching has not frayed and the soles are still solid.
Sturdiness means something is solidly built right now, while durability means it will keep holding up through years of wear and use.
Durability means something withstands long use and damage, while indestructibility claims it can never be destroyed at all.

Toughness is raw strength against damage in the moment — a tough case shrugs off a drop today. Durability adds the dimension of time: a durable item keeps resisting wear and rough use year after year. Toughness is how hard something is to hurt; durability is how long it stays that way.

Longevity is simply long life or long service — how long something keeps going before it gives out. It says nothing about abuse. Durability specifically means holding up under wear, damage, and rough use over that time. A sheltered antique can have longevity; hiking boots need durability.

Ruggedness is a sturdy build meant for rough conditions — rugged gear is designed for mud, drops, and weather. It describes the construction. Durability describes the proven result: actually withstanding wear and damage over a long time. Rugged is how something is built; durable is how it lasts.

When the parks department needed new benches for the waterfront, the cheapest bid promised teak's look at a third of the price.
Instead of choosing from a catalog, the department bolted sample benches from four suppliers to the boardwalk and left them there for two full years.
Salt spray, skateboard grinds, August sun, and two ice storms did the judging.
The composite bench that finally won was not the prettiest; it was the one whose slats had not warped, split, or loosened after all that punishment.
The buyer's report used one word to justify the price: durability -- proof, not promises, that the bench could take years of hard public use.
